rows.name: Walt Disney Co.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee unanimously adopts a **BUY** position on DIS with a final score of **1.0**. The dominant argument carrying the majority held that Disney's layered competitive moat — encompassing irreplaceable intellectual property, high-return-on-capital theme park operations, and a streaming platform now inflecting toward sustainable double-digit operating margins — is not adequately reflected in a forward P/E of 13.81x, representing a genuinely wonderful business available at a fair price. The most significant dissent came from Mr. Greenblatt, who initially passed on the grounds that the valuation, while compressed, did not constitute a compelling bargain given historically dilutive capital allocation in streaming. This objection did not prevail because, upon deliberation, Mr. Greenblatt himself conceded that the streaming unit's margin trajectory and the parks' durable pricing power justified the current multiple, ultimately shifting his position to BUY. The Committee recommends initiating a position in DIS at current levels with moderate conviction, recognizing quality at a reasonable valuation rather than a deep discount.

rows.name: American Express Co.
rows.statement: The Committee has reached a BUY recommendation on American Express with a conviction score of 0.864. The dominant argument, advanced by Mr. Buffett and ultimately endorsed by a majority including Mr. Greenblatt and Mr. Marks, rests on the enduring competitive advantage of Amex's closed-loop network — a decades-built, two-sided platform generating superior pricing power and data advantages — available at a valuation of approximately 10.6x EV/EBIT, which the Committee judges to be a fair price for a demonstrably wonderful business. The most significant dissent came from Ms. Wood, who argued that AI-driven purchasing agents and digital finance platforms will structurally erode Amex's moat and compress margins. This view did not prevail because the Committee found, per Mr. Marks's assessment, that the disruption narrative, while directionally plausible, lacks near-term evidence of the price destruction implied and underestimates the durability of Amex's premium brand positioning. The Committee recommends initiating a position at current levels.

rows.name: Alphabet Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Furton Research Investment Committee assigns Alphabet Inc. a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.853. The dominant argument carrying the majority is that Alphabet's current valuation — approximately 17x trailing earnings — materially underprices a durable competitive franchise generating 34% operating margins, commanding 90% search market share, and accelerating through an 82% year-over-year Cloud growth inflection driven by AI infrastructure demand. Four of five committee members converged on the view that this combination of quality, growth, and reasonable valuation constitutes a compelling opportunity. The most significant dissent came from the value-discipline perspective, which argued that forward multiples of roughly 22.8x and an enterprise value exceeding $4 trillion leave insufficient margin of safety under a strict earnings-yield framework. This objection did not prevail because the committee judged it applied a static valuation lens to a business undergoing a discontinuous AI-driven transition, thereby under-weighting the probability-adjusted upside in Cloud and platform convergence. The Committee recommends initiating a BUY position at current levels.

rows.name: Honeywell International Inc.
rows.statement: The Committee assigns HON a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.818. The dominant argument carrying the majority holds that the June 2026 spin-off of Honeywell Aerospace has created a classic forced-seller mispricing event: institutional holders of the former conglomerate are indiscriminately liquidating shares of the reconstituted pure-play automation entity, depressing the stock well below intrinsic value despite genuinely attractive economics—most notably Building Automation's 27% segment margins and secular tailwinds in robotics and industrial automation. The most significant dissent came from the value-discipline perspective, which flagged $34.96 billion in debt against a $66.5 billion market capitalization and a 12.8% operating margin insufficient to constitute a durable competitive moat. This concern did not prevail because the majority judged the leverage to be already reflected in the compressed valuation and manageable given the business's cash-generation profile. The Committee recommends accumulating a position in HON at current levels, with the spinoff-driven dislocation providing an asymmetric risk-reward opportunity that warrants timely action.

rows.name: Amazon.com Inc.
rows.statement: The Committee has resolved to issue a BUY recommendation on AMZN with a composite score of 0.724. The dominant argument carrying the majority centered on Amazon's positioning as a critical infrastructure provider for the AI buildout, with AWS's accelerating AI workload revenue, a $220 billion capex commitment, proprietary Trainium chip development, and durable competitive moats across cloud, advertising, and marketplace operations combining to justify the current valuation. The most significant dissent came from members applying traditional value frameworks, who argued that at a $2.83 trillion enterprise value, normalized owner earnings remain difficult to project with confidence and that the capital intensity of the retail segment dilutes overall returns on invested capital. This dissent did not prevail because the Committee judged that backward-looking earnings metrics inadequately capture the compounding value of AWS's AI infrastructure position and the margin expansion trajectory demonstrated under current management. The Committee recommends initiating a BUY position at current levels, with ongoing review of capex return realization as the primary monitoring criterion.

rows.name: Salesforce Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee adopts a BUY position on Salesforce, Inc. with a conviction score of 0.704. The dominant argument carrying the majority held that Salesforce's significant valuation compression — from approximately 37x to 16x forward earnings — has already discounted substantial uncertainty around the company's AI transition, while the underlying franchise retains formidable competitive advantages: 80% gross margins, $14.4 billion in free cash flow, and deeply embedded switching costs across the enterprise installed base. The Agentforce initiative, though early-stage, positions Salesforce as the natural enterprise deployment layer for autonomous AI agents. The most significant dissent, advanced by members applying strict value and special-situation frameworks, argued that Agentforce's revenue contribution remains speculative and that current earnings yield does not yet compensate for execution risk against Microsoft and emerging competitors. This dissent did not prevail because the majority judged that the market has already priced in considerable skepticism, creating asymmetric upside should even modest Agentforce adoption materialize. The Committee recommends initiating a position at current levels.

rows.name: Visa Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns Visa a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.69. The dominant argument, which carried a clear majority, is that Visa operates a virtually unrivaled toll-booth franchise on global commerce — connecting roughly 12 billion endpoints across 200+ countries with 66%+ operating margins and near-zero credit risk — whose self-reinforcing network effects and expanding value-added services justify a premium valuation even at 34x trailing earnings. The most significant dissent came from members who argued that at current multiples, Visa's excellence is already fully priced, and that emerging disruption from closed-loop digital wallets, A2A rails, and stablecoin settlement networks could structurally erode transaction share. This dissent did not prevail because the Committee found persuasive evidence that Visa is actively integrating these alternative rails through its "network of networks" infrastructure rather than being displaced by them. The Committee recommends initiating a position in Visa at current levels, recognizing superior business quality with moderate but acceptable valuation risk.

rows.name: Sherwin-Williams Co.
rows.statement: The Committee has resolved to issue a BUY recommendation on Sherwin-Williams Co. with a conviction score of 0.667. The dominant argument, advanced by Messrs. Buffett and Marks and carrying the majority, holds that Sherwin-Williams possesses a durable competitive moat rooted in its vertically integrated, company-owned store network, deep professional contractor loyalty, and formidable switching costs — qualities that justify a premium valuation and support reliable long-term compounding. The most significant dissent came from Mr. Greenblatt, who argued that at 27–28x earnings and approximately 20x EBITDA, the market is already pricing the moat in full, leaving insufficient margin of safety for attractive forward returns. This objection was acknowledged as substantive but did not prevail, as the majority concluded that the business's exceptional durability and pricing power warrant the current multiple over a reasonable holding period. Ms. Wood's innovation-platform objection was noted but deemed inapplicable to the thesis. The Committee recommends initiating a position at current levels.

rows.name: Home Depot Inc.
rows.statement: The Committee has reached a final position of **BUY** on Home Depot Inc. (HD), with a conviction score of **0.65**. The dominant argument carrying the majority, advanced principally by Mr. Buffett and supported by Mr. Marks, holds that Home Depot's commanding 52% share of U.S. home improvement retail, durable pricing power, and entrenched Pro contractor relationships constitute a genuine economic moat, and that current valuation at approximately 18.9–21x forward earnings adequately compensates for near-term housing cycle headwinds. The most significant dissent came from Mr. Greenblatt, who argued that the stock's full valuation and negative book equity from aggressive buybacks and acquisition debt diminish the margin of safety his framework requires; this view did not prevail because the majority concluded that conventional balance sheet metrics understate the business's true owner-earnings power and that cyclical headwinds are already reflected in the price. The Committee recommends initiating a BUY position in HD at current levels.

rows.name: McDonald's Corp.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns McDonald's a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.619. The dominant argument, advanced by Warren Buffett and seconded by Howard Marks, held that McDonald's 95% franchised model constitutes a durable royalty stream generating 46% operating margins on minimal deployed capital, and that at 17–19x forward earnings the stock remains reasonably priced for a business of this quality. The most significant dissent came from Joel Greenblatt, who acknowledged the franchise model's excellence but argued that McDonald's superiority is universally recognized and therefore fully reflected in the current valuation, leaving insufficient margin of safety for a compelling entry. This dissent did not prevail because the majority concluded, per Marks's second-level analysis, that the market has not yet fully priced in the compounding durability of the earnings stream at current multiples. The Committee recommends initiating a position in MCD at prevailing prices, with sizing appropriate to the moderate conviction level.

rows.name: NVIDIA Corp.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee adopts a BUY position on NVIDIA at a conviction score of 0.586. The majority was carried by the argument, advanced most forcefully by Mr. Aschenbrenner and Ms. Wood, that NVIDIA's compute infrastructure occupies a singular, rate-limiting position in an AI buildout whose revenue trajectory remains materially underpriced by conventional models — a thesis supported by Mr. Aschenbrenner's prior revenue forecasts having materialized with notable accuracy. The most significant dissent came from Mr. Buffett, Mr. Marks, and Mr. Greenblatt, who collectively cautioned that at a $5.45 trillion market cap and approximately 18× revenue, the stock prices perfection across a decade-long horizon, exposing holders to asymmetric downside should margins compress or custom silicon alternatives gain traction. This dissent did not prevail because the majority judged that standard mean-reversion frameworks inadequately capture the exponential demand dynamics of frontier AI infrastructure. The Committee recommends initiating a BUY position with disciplined sizing commensurate with the elevated valuation risk acknowledged by the minority.

rows.name: Microsoft Corp.
rows.statement: After full deliberation, the Committee assigns Microsoft Corporation (MSFT) a final position of **BUY** with a composite score of **0.538**. The dominant argument carrying the majority, advanced principally by Mr. Aschenbrenner and Ms. Wood, holds that Microsoft occupies the central enterprise position in a generational AI platform shift—Azure's $100 billion milestone, 41% growth rate, and the vast Copilot monetization runway across 400 million-plus M365 seats represent a regime-change opportunity that conventional valuation frameworks systematically underweight. The most significant dissent, articulated by Mr. Buffett, Mr. Marks, and Mr. Greenblatt, contended that at approximately 25 times forward earnings and nearly $4 trillion in market capitalization, the market has already priced decisive AI victory, leaving inadequate margin of safety. This dissent did not prevail because the Committee judged the probability-weighted upside from AI platform economics—particularly the compounding nature of cloud and software seat expansion—sufficient to justify the premium at current levels. The Committee recommends initiating a BUY position with disciplined sizing reflecting the narrow margin of safety acknowledged by the dissenting members.

rows.name: Johnson & Johnson
rows.statement:
## Furton Research Investment Committee — Official Statement

**Investment: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) | Final Position: BUY | Score: 0.312**

After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns a BUY rating to Johnson & Johnson with a score of 0.312, reflecting moderate conviction. The dominant argument, advanced by Howard Marks and carrying the majority, holds that at 21x forward earnings the stock offers a meaningful margin of safety for a business generating $21 billion in free cash flow, with durable competitive advantages in pharmaceuticals, MedTech, and branded consumer health — and that the talc liability, while real, is substantially reflected in the current price. The most significant dissent came from Warren Buffett and Joel Greenblatt, who argued that an above-average business trading at an above-average price fails to meet their threshold for compelling value, and that forward earnings estimates may not materialize cleanly. This dissent did not prevail because the Committee judged that J&J's quality, cash generation, and defensive positioning in a risk-elevated market cycle warranted a modest allocation. The Committee recommends initiating a measured position at current levels.

rows.name: UnitedHealth Group Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns UnitedHealth Group a BUY rating with a composite score of 0.312, reflecting a narrow and qualified majority. The dominant argument, advanced principally by Mr. Marks, held that the convergence of DOJ investigation risk, CEO transition, and medical loss ratio deterioration has driven UNH to a forward P/E of approximately 20x — a valuation that adequately discounts near-term headwinds for a business generating $23.6 billion in trailing free cash flow with durable competitive moats. The most significant dissent, articulated by Mr. Buffett and echoed by Mr. Greenblatt and Ms. Wood, cautioned that forward earnings estimates built on already-reduced management guidance remain unreliable, that structural regulatory and margin pressures may prove secular rather than cyclical, and that the stock does not yet meet a rigorous margin-of-safety standard. This dissent did not prevail because the majority judged the company-specific discount sufficient relative to intrinsic value. The Committee recommends initiating a modest position with disciplined downside monitoring tied to medical cost ratio trends and DOJ developments.
